# AMD Technical Report (as of 2026-11-19)

## 1. Data integrity notes

- **Source of truth:** every price and indicator figure below comes from the verified snapshot for 2026-11-19. The individual indicator pulls matched it for the 50 SMA, 200 SMA, RSI, MACD, Bollinger upper and lower bands, and ATR. I found no discrepancies.
- **Tool-only values:** VWMA (501.61) comes only from the indicator tool, because the snapshot doesn't list it. The 10 EMA (513.72), Bollinger middle (513.70), MACD signal (-11.96) and MACD histogram (+2.13) come only from the snapshot, because I didn't pull them separately.
- **Latest bar caution:** the 2026-11-19 volume (70,675,763) is not rounded the way earlier rows are. I can't tell whether this bar is final or still updating. If it changes, RSI, MACD, ATR and the Bollinger bands will shift slightly.

## 2. Indicators selected and why

Eight indicators were chosen to cover different information, without redundancy:

| Role | Indicator |
|---|---|
| Medium- and long-term trend | `close_50_sma`, `close_200_sma` |
| Momentum and trend change | `macd` (with signal and histogram from the snapshot) |
| Overbought/oversold | `rsi` |
| Volatility envelope | `boll_ub`, `boll_lb` |
| Risk sizing | `atr` |
| Volume-confirmed trend | `vwma` |

## 3. Latest price action (2026-11-19)

- **Bar:** open 543.48, high 555.01, low 470.56, close 489.19, on volume of 70.68M.
- **Reversal shape:** AMD gapped up from the prior close of 530.14 (2026-11-18), then sold off through the day. It closed 40.95 lower than the previous close and in the bottom quarter of the day's range (about 22% from the low).
- **Volume:** this is one of the two heaviest sessions in the six-month data pulled. The other is 2026-11-05 at 71.24M, when the close was 404.40. A high-volume down-reversal after a gap-up is a bearish signal.
- **The 50 SMA coincidence:** the intraday high of 555.01 sits almost exactly on the 50 SMA (554.93). That is an observation only, not a validated resistance level.

## 4. Trend structure

**Moving averages**
- **50 SMA:** 554.93, essentially flat. It was 539.54 on 2026-10-20 and 555.22 on 2026-11-18. Price at 489.19 is below it by about 65.7 points.
- **200 SMA:** 428.63 and rising steadily, from 397.42 on 2026-10-20. Price is about 60.6 points above it.
- **50 over 200:** the 50 SMA is well above the 200 SMA, so the long-term structure is still constructive. I can't date when that crossover occurred.
- **200 SMA breach on 2026-11-05:** the close of 404.40 was below the 200 SMA of 415.00 that day. The next day (2026-11-06), the close of 449.04 was back above it (415.98). So the long-term average was briefly lost and quickly reclaimed.
- **10 EMA:** 513.72, with price below it. Short-term trend is down.

**Net read:** the trend is mixed. It is bullish long-term (above a rising 200 SMA) but weak near-term (below the 10 EMA and 50 SMA). This is a pullback or consolidation inside a larger uptrend, not a clean downtrend.

**Price path context**
- The highest close in the window is 649.42 on 2026-10-06 (high 658.52).
- Early October to mid-November shows a drawdown with violent swings. Closes went 578.44 (2026-10-28), 404.40 (2026-11-05), 585.30 (2026-11-12) and 489.19 (2026-11-19).
- The 2026-11-12 high of 594.00 did not reclaim the October high.

## 5. Momentum

- **MACD:** -9.83, signal -11.96, histogram +2.13. The MACD line is slightly above its signal, but both are below zero, so this is a weak, bear-market-style bullish crossover.
- **MACD path:** it troughed at -30.20 on 2026-11-06 and recovered to -8.03 on 2026-11-18. Today it ticked back down to -9.83. The recovery in momentum stalled with today's reversal.
- **RSI:** 45.16, down from 50.34 the day before. It touched 29.75 on 2026-11-05, close to oversold. Its highest reading in this window was 57.48 on 2026-11-12. RSI has not reached overbought and has stayed in a sub-60 range, which fits a market with no sustained upside momentum.
- **Divergence:** I won't claim a formal divergence, because the tool output doesn't clearly support one.

## 6. Volatility and risk (Bollinger and ATR)

- **Bollinger bands:** upper 602.60, middle 513.70, lower 424.80, so the bands are about 178 points wide. Price at 489.19 sits in the lower half of the range (about 0.36 of the way from lower to upper).
- **Band direction:** the upper band has fallen from 677.35 (2026-10-22) to 602.60, so the old high-volatility rally is rolling out of the window. The lower band dropped sharply after the 2026-11-05 crash, from 498.27 (2026-10-23) to 424.80.
- **ATR:** 43.48, up from about 26.0 on 2026-10-29, an increase of roughly 67%. That is about 8.9% of the current close, so daily ranges are very large.
- **Implication:** stops must be wide and position sizes small. For reference, 1.5× ATR is about 65 points (about 424 from the current close) and 2× ATR is about 87 points (about 402). These are arithmetic reference levels only.

## 7. Volume confirmation (VWMA)

- **VWMA:** 501.61, with price below it by about 12 points.
- **Trend:** it fell from 593.99 (2026-10-20) to about 492 by 2026-11-09 and has flattened around 500–506 since. It sits well below the 50 SMA (about 53 points), which suggests heavy volume has been concentrated on lower-price days (for example 2026-10-30, 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-05).
- **Read:** volume-weighted trading is below the simple average, so volume has favored sellers during the pullback. Today's heavy-volume decline reinforces that.

## 8. Reference levels (observational, not validated)

I did not verify any historical bounces or rejections at these levels.

**Overhead**
- ~501.6 – 504: VWMA, plus the 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17 closes (504.28 and 503.41).
- ~513.7: 10 EMA and Bollinger middle, nearly identical.
- ~530.1: 2026-11-18 close, the last close before today's gap-and-fade.
- ~555: 50 SMA, also today's intraday high.
- ~585–594: 2026-11-12 close (585.30) and high (594.00).

**Below**
- 470.56: today's low.
- 449.04 / 433.30: 2026-11-06 close and low.
- ~425–429: lower Bollinger band (424.80) and 200 SMA (428.63), a confluence of indicator levels.
- 402.10 / 404.40: 2026-11-05 low and close.

## 9. Scenarios

- **Bearish/cautious (current lean):** today's reversal on very heavy volume, together with price below the 10 EMA, VWMA and 50 SMA, favors further weakness or a retest of the lows. A close below 470.56 would open the ~425–429 confluence zone, where the 200 SMA is the key long-term trend line. A close below the 200 SMA would damage the constructive long-term structure.
- **Neutral/range:** with RSI mid-40s and MACD near zero, price may oscillate between roughly 470 and 514 while volatility settles.
- **Bullish recovery:** this needs a close back above 513–514 (10 EMA and Bollinger middle), ideally with MACD turning up from its slightly negative level and RSI back above 50. A move toward the 50 SMA (~555) would then be the next test. Today's failure near that average argues for patience.

**Risk management:** ATR near 43 and recent swings of 8–17% in single sessions (for example 488.78 to 404.40 on 2026-11-05) argue for reduced size and wide, volatility-based stops. Gap risk is high.

**Data availability (read first).** Only one of the three sources returned data. The Yahoo Finance news feed failed (YFDataException) and the Reddit fetch failed for r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks and r/investing. Neither failure says anything about AMD, and I have not estimated or filled in either source. The read below rests on one StockTwits snapshot of 20 on-topic messages, all timestamped within roughly 20 minutes of each other (about 21:38–21:55 UTC on 2026-11-19). That is a narrow sample taken in the middle of a sharp move, so confidence is low.

**1. StockTwits breakdown (20 messages, "Screened by Jev")**
- The classifier's stance read is 6 bullish, 5 bearish, 2 neutral and 7 unclear, which is close to evenly split.
- The user tags are Bullish 5 (25%), Bearish 3 (15%) and unlabeled 12 (60%). Among tagged posts that is 62.5% bullish to 37.5% bearish, but on only 8 tagged posts. That is too small to treat as a real ratio.
- The tags and the post text do not line up well. Several "Bullish" posts are defensive rather than a fresh bullish thesis:
  - @omega8119 asks "Have people figured out the report was a scam yet?"
  - @shonv says "Todays news was false" and predicts "$500.X tomorrow".
  - @Ashton_1nvests relays AMD's denial of the short report.
  - @bbox2haejo and @Lucy888 are low-content ("mommy Lisa", or a bare cashtag).
- Several unlabeled posts are clearly distressed:
  - @RAMS_SB_2022: "down another 10 AF. 479 WTF?!?!?!?!?"
  - @Masontrade88: "wtf"
  - @adamsjay333: "Any chance this drops below $300?"
  - @humbletrader8: "another POS in the sector"
  - @ShadowBanningIsBad: "100x over priced" and "drops 15% and it takes the market with it"
- The bearish tags are mixed in quality:
  - @RedWhiteBlue200: "short term bearish. Long term will be fine."
  - @Franking71: "under $300.00"
  - @Tillraysucks: "sell lisa su a spy"
- Dip-buying appears once: @SimplifiedTrader writes "started a good day 550 to this buy the dip".
- @Jdogg85 posts "ill buy at $25", which reads as trolling or hyperbole.
- @GTA_Terminal reports dark-pool volume for Wed Nov 18 (before the drop). It was 18.3M shares, 53.9% of volume and 1.1x normal, against a 49.2% average and a five-session average of 20.8M. The bot labels this neutral. It says nothing about the Nov 19 selloff.
- The price levels quoted are inconsistent: ~550 at the open, 479 at the latest print, and "under $300" or "below $300" in other posts. I can't verify any of them. The $300 posts may be hyperbole or errors. I would not treat them as price data.

**2. Cross-source divergence.** There is none to measure, because news and Reddit are missing. Within StockTwits there is a divergence between the user tags (mildly bullish by count) and the tone and price context (shock, a roughly 10–15% intraday drop, retail sentiment under stress). The bullish tags look like a reflexive "hold the line" defense and not conviction buying.

**3. Dominant narrative themes**
- **Hunterbrook short report (Nov 19).** This is the main driver. As relayed in posts, it alleges issues around AMD's business practices and relationships, with an export-control angle. AMD responded: "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," and said it complies with U.S. export control laws. One post says Hunterbrook disclosed a position (the text is truncated). Only the post excerpts support this. I have no news article to confirm the details.
- **China and export controls.** Posts such as "the government's job to make sure the chips didn't go to China" and "the govt isn't going to do anything to NVDA or AMD, they need them" show retail split on regulatory risk.
- **Valuation and index contagion.** Posts argue AMD is overpriced and that its fall dragged the broader market. This is opinion, and I can't verify the market move from this data.
- **Wider macro anxiety.** One post cites airlines, cyberattacks, Microsoft and a failed Anthropic IPO. These are unverified references and may be hyperbole, but they suggest a risk-off backdrop.
- **AMD vs NVDA comparisons.** Bulls reject the comparison, while others group the two together on regulatory exposure.
- **Management trust.** There are several Lisa Su references, both affectionate and as a jab.

**4. Catalysts and risks**
- Further disclosure or follow-up from Hunterbrook, or any regulatory or government response on export controls.
- Further AMD statements, or evidence refuting the report. Bulls expect a rebound, but this is retail speculation and not an event.
- Possible forced selling and momentum effects after a double-digit drop. Retail is already asking about lower levels.
- Broader risk-off and index-level contagion, if the drop is as market-moving as claimed.
- Because the news and Reddit sources failed, I can't say whether institutional coverage is more or less negative than retail.

**5. Summary table**

| Signal | Direction | Source | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overall retail stance split | Mixed | StockTwits (Jev screen) | 6 bull / 5 bear / 2 neutral / 7 unclear of 20 on-topic |
| User-tagged ratio | Mildly bullish (weak) | StockTwits | 5 bull (25%), 3 bear (15%), 12 unlabeled; only 8 tagged |
| Short-report shock | Bearish | StockTwits | Hunterbrook report; "down another 10 AF. 479"; "drops 15%" |
| Company rebuttal | Mildly bullish | StockTwits | AMD: "claims misrepresent AMD's business practices"; says it complies with export controls |
| Dip-buy / hold defiance | Bullish (low quality) | StockTwits | "report was a scam", "$500.X tomorrow", "buy the dip" |
| Valuation and contagion complaints | Bearish | StockTwits | "100x over priced", "took the market with it" |
| Regulatory and China risk | Bearish / uncertain | StockTwits | Export-control comments; "govt…need them" |
| Dark-pool activity (Nov 18) | Neutral | StockTwits (@GTA_Terminal) | 18.3M shares, 53.9% of volume, 1.1x normal; predates the drop |
| News headlines | Unavailable | Yahoo Finance | YFDataException; not estimated |
| Reddit discussion | Unavailable | Reddit | Fetch failed; not an absence of discussion |

**Bottom line:** The evidence is a mixed, event-driven retail reaction to a short report and a sharp price drop. Tags lean slightly bullish, while tone and price action lean bearish and stressed. With only 20 messages from one platform in a ~20-minute window, and no news or Reddit data, this is a weak signal for the trader to weigh with fundamentals, technicals and verified reporting on the Hunterbrook claims. It is not a price call.

# AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.) Fundamental Analysis, as of 2026-11-19

**Scope and data caveats**
- Sources are the five tools: fundamentals snapshot, quarterly balance sheet, cash flow, income statement, and insider transactions. No news, guidance, or segment data was available.
- The quarterly statements have no December quarters (Q4), and cash flow is reported year-to-date. I de-cumulated the cash flow figures myself. Q4 2025 values are only implied from the TTM figures.
- Total liabilities and debt are not tagged in the balance sheet feed. Liabilities below are derived as assets minus equity.
- The current price is not given directly. I inferred about $489 from P/E 104.53 × EPS 4.68, P/B 11.73 × book value 41.70, and market cap divided by about 1.655B shares. All three agree.

---

## 1. Snapshot and valuation

| Metric | Value | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Market cap | ~$809.6B | |
| Implied price | ~$489 | About 26% below the 52-week high of $658.52 and about 160% above the low of $188.22 |
| Trailing P/E (GAAP) | 104.5x | EPS (TTM) $4.68 |
| Forward P/E | 27.7x | Forward EPS $17.64, about 3.8x TTM EPS |
| PEG | 0.47 | Depends entirely on the forward growth assumption |
| P/B | 11.7x | Book value is $41.70 per share |
| P/S (TTM) | ~17.8x | Revenue TTM $45.4B |
| FCF yield | ~0.9% | FCF TTM $7.36B, per the fundamentals feed |
| Beta | 2.54 | Very high volatility |
| Dividend | 0% | |
| 50-day / 200-day average | $555 / $427 | Price is about 12% below the 50-day and about 14.5% above the 200-day |

- **Valuation gap.** The forward P/E is only 27.7x against 104.5x trailing, because forward EPS is about 3.8x TTM EPS. The latest quarterly GAAP EPS of $1.46 annualizes to about $5.84, or about 84x at the implied price.
- The forward figure is likely a non-GAAP, next-year estimate. The market is therefore pricing a steep earnings ramp that has not yet appeared in reported GAAP results.
- **Price trend.** The stock sits between the 200-day and 50-day averages after a pullback from its high. Beta of 2.54 means large swings in either direction.

---

## 2. Income statement: growth and operating leverage

| Quarter | Revenue ($M) | Gross margin | Operating income ($M) | Op. margin | Net income ($M) | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q3 FY25 (Sep-25) | 9,246 | 51.7% | 1,270 | 13.7% | 1,243 | $0.75 |
| Q1 FY26 (Mar-26) | 10,253 | 52.8% | 1,476 | 14.4% | 1,383 | $0.84 |
| Q2 FY26 (Jun-26) | 11,536 | 53.8% | 1,990 | 17.3% | 2,297 | $1.38 |
| **Q3 FY26 (Sep-26)** | **13,377** | **53.9%** | **2,832** | **21.2%** | **2,428** | **$1.46** |

- **Revenue growth.** Q3 FY26 revenue is up 44.7% YoY and 16.0% sequentially. Q2 was up about 50% YoY and Q1 about 38%, so growth is sustained and accelerating in dollar terms. Revenue has risen from $5.9B in Q1 2022 to $13.4B.
- **Gross margin.** It has expanded about 220 bp YoY and has plateaued near 54% over the last two quarters.
- **Operating leverage.** Opex is about $4.38B, up about 25% YoY against 45% revenue growth. Opex fell from 38% of revenue to 32.7% in a year. The incremental YoY operating margin is about 38% (+$1.56B operating income on +$4.13B revenue).
- **Earnings quality.** In Q2 FY26, net income ($2,297M) exceeded operating income ($1,990M), which implies a tax benefit or other income. Q3 is cleaner, with net income at about 86% of operating income. Treat Q2 EPS of $1.38 as possibly flattered.
- **TTM and implied Q4.** TTM revenue is $45.4B and TTM net income is $7.7B (16.8% margin). That implies Q4 FY25 revenue of about $10.3B and net income of about $1.6B.
- **Comparison base.** Q2 FY25 operating income was −$134M, which reflects a one-off charge (my inference, not stated in the feed). It makes YoY comparisons for that quarter look especially strong.

---

## 3. Balance sheet

| ($M) | Q3 FY25 | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total assets | 76,926 | 79,642 | 84,464 | **94,812** |
| Current assets | 26,947 | 28,628 | 31,522 | 39,471 |
| Cash & equivalents | 5,585 | 5,086 | 5,086* | 7,404 |
| Current liabilities | 9,455 | 10,506 | 12,081 | 14,486 |
| Stockholders' equity | 64,462 | 67,224 | 67,224* | 68,389 |
| Derived liabilities (assets − equity) | ~12.5B | ~12.4B | ~17.2B | **~26.4B** |

*The columns shown are an approximate rather than exact alignment for the intermediate quarters. The Q2→Q3 comparison (assets 84,464 → 94,812; equity 67,224 → 68,389; cash 5,086 → 7,404) is read directly from the final columns and is reliable.

- **Quarterly balance sheet jump.** Total assets rose about $10.3B in one quarter. Current assets rose about $7.9B, and cash accounts for only about $2.3B of that.
- The rest is likely receivables and inventory building for the ramp, but the feed does not break it out.
- Derived liabilities rose about $9.2B, from roughly $17.2B to $26.4B. Implied non-current liabilities more than doubled, from about $5.2B to about $11.9B.
- Equity rose only about $1.2B. The expansion was funded by liabilities rather than equity.
- **Leverage.** The fundamentals feed shows debt/equity of 13.5% and a current ratio of 2.73. On about $68B of equity, 13.5% implies roughly $9B of debt, well above AMD's historical levels (my inference, not confirmed). The feed is also not clear whether the ratio uses the latest quarter.
- **Goodwill legacy.** The 2022 step-change in assets ($12.4B to $66.9B) and equity ($7.5B to $55.3B) reflects the Xilinx acquisition. This explains the low ROE (12.0%) and ROA (5.9%) and the high P/B. Large acquisition intangibles also depress GAAP earnings relative to non-GAAP.

---

## 4. Cash flow: the main caution flag

De-cumulated from the year-to-date figures ($M):

| | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | 9M FY26 | 9M FY25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Operating cash flow | 2,955 | 2,366 | **1,202** | 6,523 | 5,109 |
| Capex | 389 | 808 | 648 | 1,845 | 752 |
| **Free cash flow** | 2,566 | 1,558 | **554** | 4,678 | 4,357 |
| Investing cash flow | −2,565 | −2,850 | −1,243 | −6,658 | −3,992 |

- If forward EPS landed at $11.68 (double the Q3 annualized figure), the forward P/E would be about 42x. That is not cheap for a company that already trades at 17.8x sales.
- Q2 net income exceeded operating income ($2,297M vs $1,990M), so that quarter's EPS is probably flattered. Net income rose only 5.7% sequentially in Q3 while revenue rose 16%. The 123% operating income growth you cite is the best line on the income statement, not the bottom line.

Current assets rose about $7.9B in Q3 and cash explains only $2.3B of that. That leaves about $5.6B of non-cash assets added in one quarter, against only $1.84B of sequential revenue growth.

## 6. The short report and the blind spot

- You're right that an allegation isn't a finding. But markets don't wait for findings. Export-control scrutiny can drag on for months, and a stock at 104x trailing with a beta of 2.54 has no cushion for an overhang.

We also don't know what caused the 17% crash on Nov 5. Two violent moves in two weeks, both with unexplained catalysts, is a risk in itself.

## 7. Insiders: your denominator is wrong

- Comparing Su's roughly $248M of 2026 sales to a $810B market cap is meaningless. The relevant comparison is her sales against her holdings, which the feed doesn't give us.

Su sold 70,000 shares ($35.5M) on Nov 16, and Norrod sold an additional 10,000 on top of his usual monthly pattern, both three days before today's drop. I'm not alleging anything improper. But if the export-control issue grows, the optics will matter.

## 8. Competition and macro

The research has no competitive data, so this part is general knowledge and not from the provided files. AMD's roughly 54% gross margin sits well below the market leader in AI accelerators. That leader also has a software moat (CUDA), and large customers are building in-house chips. Without segment data, I can't tell you how much of the revenue growth is AI accelerators or how concentrated the customer base is.

On macro, 98% odds of no Fed cuts means no multiple support. The 10-year yield, VIX and CPI are unavailable, so the "steady backdrop" claim rests on prediction markets alone. A 2% recession probability reads as complacency, not safety.

## Where I could be wrong

- The 10-Q shows the working capital build is benign and FCF rebounds in Q4.
- The $17.64 forward EPS turns out to be conservative on a GAAP-comparable basis.
- The Hunterbrook claims are refuted and the export-control overhang clears.

I'd also note that your own tripwire (FCF falling while revenue growth slows) requires two bad things at once. By the time both are visible, the stock will be well below 489.

## Bottom line

I would not treat the 425–470 zone as a dip to buy. It sits one ATR from the 200 SMA, and the 200 SMA has already been breached once. Risk/reward is poor: a stop at the 200 SMA (about 428) is roughly 12% below today's close, and an ATR-based stop would be wider. The upside depends on a forward EPS number we can't verify. I'd stay underweight or on the sidelines until the 10-Q resolves the cash flow and balance sheet questions, the export-control story clarifies, and price reclaims the 10 EMA and 50 SMA.
